title: When comfort becomes hard to release
meaning: Care for your home can bind you to familiar comforts when every improvement demands more things and effort.
text: Your shared routine can centre on small pleasures: soft lighting, good food and objects that make daily life comfortable. The Empress in the physical position of Muladhara describes creating this tangible comfort. In energy, the same card tests your footing through excess: you want to keep furnishing and providing, as though there is never quite enough. The Devil in emotions describes attachment to the comfort you have gained. Giving up part of it can feel like too great a loss, even when home is becoming crowded.

For example, you choose a new coffee machine although the old one still works. Cups, a shelf and supplies of favourite coffee follow; the morning ritual gradually occupies the whole kitchen. **A domestic pleasure can demand more room than you want to give it.** Your enjoyment of the purchase is real, yet it brings an entire arrangement to maintain. Even a simple breakfast becomes difficult to imagine differently, and clearing the table can feel almost like a deprivation.

The vulnerable point appears when discussing spending or surplus possessions makes you hold more tightly to what is familiar. You try to preserve a feeling of provision by buying something else or defending each purchase. Effort then goes into maintaining comfort, while your freedom to choose narrows. Home can feel freer when enjoying things also allows a decision to add nothing more.
